unite_adi: UPPER SECONDARY-PREP YEAR-LEVEL: B1 - THEME 13: LIFE IN THE NEIGHBOURHOOD, CITY AND SOCIAL LIFE

bolumler.ogrenmeKanitlari: PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT: Students will design a detailed project exploring the cultural and historical places, festivals and events, and problems in their neighbourhood and city. The project will start by identifying significant cultural and historical sites, such as monuments, museums, or landmarks, and explaining their importance to the community. Students will also research festivals and events that take place in their area, discussing how these celebrations bring people together and reflect local traditions. Additionally, the project will focus on identifying common problems in the neighbourhood and city, such as traffic, pollution, or lack of public spaces, and students will propose practical solutions to address these issues. The project will include a written report summarising the findings, supported by visuals such as photographs, maps, or charts to enhance the presentation. Students are encouraged to interview local residents or use other resources to gather more insights into the topics. Along with the report, students will prepare a short oral presentation to share their findings with the class, focusing on the most interesting cultural or historical aspects, key festivals, and the proposed solutions to local problems. The assignment will be evaluated by using rubrics. Öğrenme-Öğretme Yaşantıları
bolumler.temelKabuller: This theme includes the concept of ''life in the neighbourhood and city & social life with its components such as cultural and historical places in the neighbourhood and the city; festivals and events in the neighbourhood and the city; problems in the neighbourhood and the city'' and it is assumed that it could be present in almost all languages, with some exceptions. It is assumed that a student in the preparatory year of an upper secondary school may know what cultural and historical places in the neighbourhood and the city; festivals and events in the neighbourhood and the city; problems in the neighbourhood and the city mean in their own language as it is known that almost all people who start to learn a new language bring their pre-existing knowledge (in their own language) with them and transfer it to their new language learning context. However, they may not know how to say these things in another language if this has not yet been covered in their existing curriculum. Fortunately, this existing knowledge in their own language can help them recognise, understand, and learn them more easily in a foreign language, in this case English. As they are students in the preparatory year of an upper secondary school, they are expected to know some basic vocabulary about ''life in the neighbourhood and city & social life'' in English from previous themes and/ or years such as ''a sightseeing place, a historical ruin, to visit, to celebrate, etc.'' and also some structures such as ''How can I go to the museum in the city centre? They must clean the streets regularly.'' in English from the previous themes and/or years. These grammar items and vocabulary are revised during the ''Revision Programme'' at the beginning of the year and they can be used as a basis for learning the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme, so that the new grammatical elements in the current theme can be learnt easily.
bolumler.onDegerlendirme: It is assumed that these students in the preparatory year of an upper secondary school are ready to learn the concept of ''cultural and historical places in the neighbourhood and the city; festivals and events in the neighbourhood and the city; problems in the neighbourhood and the city'' cognitively, affectively, and socially since it is appropriate to their age and language level. Therefore, a contextual picture could be provided for the students to remember and practise the items that they are related and previously learnt so that they can discuss the picture in pairs and write down what they remember. This session can help them revise all the related vocabulary and grammatical elements that they have already learnt from previous themes or from previous years as a preparatory practice. In this way, their performance can be evaluated in terms of how much they remember and how accurately they use these items to build their competence in the current theme. It can help the teacher decide what to emphasise, revise, and practise in order to facilitate the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme. (Their performance can be evaluated by rubrics, a rating scale, and /or a marking scheme during these practices.).
bolumler.zenginlestirme: Objective: To talk about cultural and historical places, festivals/events, and city problems in English for enhancing critical thinking and speaking skills. Activity 1: Listen, Analyse, and Debate The teacher provides a detailed listening text describing cultural and historical places, festivals/events, and city problems, along with visuals representing these elements. Students listen carefully and analyse the key points or themes in the descriptions (e.g., the importance of preserving historical landmarks, the significance of cultural festivals, or solutions to urban problems) and then they categorise them. After sequencing the visuals based on the text, students form groups to discuss and debate topics such as ''Why are cultural festivals important for community identity?'', or ''What are the most effective ways to solve city problems like pollution or overcrowding?''. The teacher facilitates the discussion, encouraging students to use target vocabulary and supporting their critical thinking skills. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity. Objective: To talk about cultural and historical places, festivals/events, and city problems in English for improving collaborative speaking and problem-solving skills. Objective: To talk about cultural and historical places, festivals/events, and city problems in English by using the target vocabulary and the target grammar. Activity 2: Role-Play: City Council Meeting The teacher gives each student a role, such as city mayor, environmentalist, cultural heritage expert, local resident, or event organiser. Students receive simple instructions about their role and concerns (e.g., preserving a historical building, planning a festival, or solving traffic problems). In small groups, they act as members of a city council and discuss these issues. Each student shares their ideas, explains their concerns, and suggests solutions. The group works together to decide on the best solution for the issue. The teacher monitors and gives feedback on target vocabulary usage and how well students communicate their ideas. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
bolumler.destekleme: Objective: To talk about cultural and historical places, festivals/events, and city problems in English by using the target vocabulary and the target grammar. Activity 1: Explore and Match The teacher prepares digital or physical cards with pictures of cultural and historical places (e.g., mosques, museums, castles), festivals/events (e.g., carnivals, concerts, parades), and city problems (e.g., traffic, litter, air pollution) along with cards displaying their names. Students first match each picture with its correct name. After matching, they create sentences using the target grammar to describe each category (e.g., ''There is a beautiful mosque in our neighbourhood'', ''We will celebrate the carnival next month'', ''Traffic is a big problem in the city'', ''What can/should we do for the problems?'', ''What can be done to solve this problem?''). The teacher provides feedback on grammar and pronunciation, ensuring the sentences are clear and correctly structured. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity. Objective: To identify cultural and historical places, festivals/events, and city problems in English by using the target vocabulary and the target grammar. Activity 2: Listen and Order The teacher provides visuals depicting cultural and historical places, festivals/events, and city problems and plays a listening text describing these elements in a sequence. Students listen carefully and arrange the visuals in the order mentioned in the text. After sequencing the visuals, they describe the sequence using sentences in the target grammar (e.g., ''There is an ancient castle near the city'', ''Next week, the city will host a cultural festival'', ''Traffic is one of the main problems in the neighbourhood'', ''What can/should we do for the problems?'', ''What can be done to solve this problem?''). The teacher provides feedback on their grammar, pronunciation, and clarity of expression. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
